marks.q: The Group is firmly on track to deliver management's expectations of full year adjusted profit before tax(1) for FY21 of c. £345m.
Excellent performance throughout the year across all business areas, with the Group expected to deliver FY21 adjusted profit before tax1  of c. £345m (FY20: £143.9m), in line with previous guidance

Housebuilding adjusted gross margin increased to 22.3% (2020: 17.6%) with the business targeting an adjusted gross margin of 23% for 2022 and firmly on track to deliver its margin target of 25% for 2025.
Our expectation for profit in the first half has moved forward, and for 2022 we expect adjusted profit before tax to be at the top end of market forecasts
Whilst we are mindful of the wider economic uncertainties, we remain positive on our outlook and continue to expect adjusted profit before tax for FY 22 to be at the top end of market forecasts
While mindful of the wider economic uncertainties, Vistry remains positive on its outlook and continues to expect adjusted profit before tax for the 2022 financial year to be approximately £417m.
Whilst we are mindful of the wider economic uncertainties, we remain positive on our outlook and continue to expect adjusted profit before tax for FY 22 to be c. £417m

2022 was another year of excellent progress for Vistry, and despite the more challenging market conditions following the September mini-budget, profits are in-line with expectations and ahead of where we were at the start of the year.

Market conditions are improving and based on the assumption that private sales rates continue to trend towards levels seen in 2019, we expect Group adjusted profit before tax for FY23 to be in excess of £440m
Reflecting the strength of the forward order book and progress on integration, the Group now expects to deliver adjusted profit before tax for FY23 in excess of £450m.

Given the strength of the Group's forward order book, the progress on integration and the Group's targeted cost savings, the Board continues to expect the Group to deliver adjusted profit before tax for FY23 in excess of £450m.
The Board re-iterates guidance of in excess of £450m adjusted profit before tax for FY23.

We estimate the FY23 impact of the reduction in full year site margins to be in the region of £40m and as a result, the Group's targeted FY23 adjusted profit before tax, including this impact, is £410m.
The Group had a strong run into the year end and I'm pleased to report that adjusted profit before tax for FY23 is anticipated to be ahead of guidance.

The Group is on track to deliver a strong growth in completions in 2024, targeting in excess of 17,500 units, underpinned by its forward sales position totalling £4.6bn, of which £2.1bn is for delivery in 2024.
We expect half year and full year profit to be ahead of last year and remain confident in achieving a 40% ROCE and £800m operating profit in the medium term.

The Group is well positioned to deliver more than 18,000 (FY23: 16,118) completions and full year profits ahead of last year in FY24, underpinned by our strong first half performance and our forward sales position.

We are encouraged by our sales performance through the typically quieter summer months and are on track to deliver a strong growth in total completions in FY24 to in excess of 18,000 (FY23: 16,118) units, and full year profits ahead of last year.

The estimated one-off impact of adjusting for the revised development cost assumptions reduces the Board's expectations for adjusted profit before tax for FY24 by c. £80m, for FY25 by c. £30m, and FY26 by c. £5m.
Group adjusted profit before tax is expected to be c. £250m (FY23: £419.1m), in-line with the revised company guidance announced in December
The Group is making good progress and continues to expect to deliver a year on year increase in profits in FY25 with, as previously guided, a more significant H2 weighting than in prior years.
In the near term, the Group remains focused on executing the strategic and cash generation initiatives laid out in March and is on track to deliver a year-on-year increase in profits in FY25.
Guidance for the full year remains unchanged with the Group expecting to deliver a year-on-year increase in profits in FY 25.
Our expectations for the year remain unchanged and the Group remains confident in delivering year-on-year profit growth for FY25.
Group adjusted profit before tax is anticipated to be around £270m (FY24: £263.5m), in line with expectations

The Group expects to deliver good year-on-year revenue and volume growth, and an improvement in adjusted profit before tax in 2026, albeit with a lower overall margin reflecting the incentives offered during the current sales initiative.
The Board expects adjusted profit before tax for FY 2026 to be towards the middle of the range of analysts' forecasts
As a result, the Board expects that adjusted profit before tax for FY 2026 will be in line with the current market consensus (Company compiled analyst consensus for 2026 is adjusted PBT of £200m).
Excluding the items above, we expect APBT to be in the region of £165m.
